All paths below are relative to C:\Users\kopiy\Downloads\Super_R-R\decompiled\CodeEntries\.

1) Hierarchy. objPlayer (idx 98) has 101 direct children (objects.tsv). Its own events do very little: Create sets energie/ammo/HotWeapon* and global.maddx/maddy; Alarm_0 sets persistent=false; Draw applies a mask-26 shader; Step contains odd objPicture camera code. No player file calls event_inherited, so in practice objPlayer works as a group tag for collisions, `objPlayer.x` reads, `with (objPlayer)` and `instance_exists(objPlayer)`. Its children fall into four groups:
- Controllable bodies: objPlayerMouse (67 rooms), objPlayerMouseHouse (32 rooms, home/store scenes), objPlayerBiker (4), objPlayerBikerHouse (child of Biker, 5), objPlayerHospital (4), objPlayerGriffin (1, rmGriffin), objPigButcher, objPlayerShieldMouse (human shield), and objPlayerController (legacy gamepad body; its Step is just `exit`).
- About 70 execution/kill cutscene objects (objPKnifeKill, objPKillFat*, objAubreyKill*, objMC*Kill, ...).
- Scripted transition bodies (objPlayerOpenWindow, objPWalkWindow, objPlayerClimbUp/Down, objPVomit, ...).
- objPlayerDead (idx 50) is NOT a child; objPlayerBombDead is its child. objPlayerBoss (962) is an AI enemy that reuses Jacket's look, not a player.

2) Input in objPlayerMouse.
- Movement: scrPlayerMoveKeyboard polls keyboard_check_direct(ord(global.leftkey/rightkey/upkey/downkey)), defaults W/A/S/D (scrTitleInit.gml:81-85), rebindable via scrLoadKeys. It uses acceleration of 0.5 per step up to myspeed (3 by default, changed by mask/sprite). Hard mode mirrors the controls; mask 20 reverses them. There are no Keyboard_W/A/S/D events on objPlayerMouse.
- Aim: dir = point_direction(x,y,global.mousex,global.mousey) (Step_0.gml:58). global.mousex/y are computed in objEffector_Draw_0.gml:75-81 from objPlayer.x plus display_mouse_get_x() offset from the screen centre (mouse_x is not used). If global.enemy is locked (objEffector_Draw_0.gml:88-92), the aim point is replaced by the enemy position.
- Shift (vk_shift, held): look-far. aimfar = keyboard_check_direct(vk_shift) (Step_0.gml:268) pushes view_xview[0] toward the cursor, and the cursor factor becomes 1.8. Shift is NOT lock-on. KeyPress_16 (Shift) and KeyPress_17 (Ctrl) only toggle `aim`, which objPlayerMouse never reads (dead variable).
- Lock-on: middle-mouse press (Mouse_55 = ev_global_middle_press). It temporarily moves the player to global.mousex/y with 2x scale to pick an objEnemy, objEnemyIdle, objEHideM16, objBoss, objPanther or objMiscEnemy into global.enemy. Pressing again clears it. Disabled in hard mode and with mask 27.
- Left mouse held (Mouse_50 = global left button): scrPlayerShoot, which handles both melee and guns, gated by reload<=0. The Step also polls mb_left for flamethrower and pig-butcher continuous fire.
- Right mouse: holding it (Mouse_51) increments `release` and calls scrPlayerPickUp2 after 20 frames (drop weapon at feet / pick up). Release (Mouse_57) with release<20 and reload<=0 calls scrPlayerPickUp (tokens, secret masks, weapon pickup/swap/throw). Right held also drives the Skippy/Igel charge (Step_0.gml:468-491).
- Space (KeyPress_32): scrKillShield = throat-stab (scrThroatEnemy), ground execution on objKnockedOut, or human shield.
- F held (Keyboard_70): Skippy punch start, mask-6 knife throw, mask-22 chainsaw sprint.
- Q held (Keyboard_81): colour-redux toggle.
- R: restart. objPlayerDead_KeyPress_82 sets endtransition; objEffector_KeyPress_82 starts the fade only if !instance_exists(objPlayer); objPlayerDead_Step_0 and objEffector_Step_0 also poll global.restartkey.
- Esc: objEffector_KeyPress_27 (pause).

3) Movement and collision: x/y are moved with place_free and corner-sliding (scrPlayerMoveKeyboard.gml:629-674). scrMoveSolidOn/Off makes soft walls and glass solid only during the player's move. There is also a lunge/recoil step via move_towards_point(impx,impy,impact) (Step_0.gml:382-391), which uses built-in speed/direction. Legs: legdir = direction of (myxspeed,myyspeed), legindex advances with speed.

4) Weapons have no id variable. The weapon is encoded in sprite_index (sprPWalkX / sprPAttackX).
- Pickup: scrGetWeapon maps objWeapon.image_index to a walk sprite and writes objPlayer.sprite_index. scrCurrentWeapon / scrCurrentWeaponExt map sprite back to index.
- Ammo is in `ammo`; heat in HotWeaponAlpha; thrown props in throwindex + sprPWalkThrow.
- Throws and drops create objWeaponThrow (image_index, direction, speed, ammo, hotalpha). Throwing weapons (index 31-37) create objThrowingWeapon (scrPlayerPickUp.gml:516-600).
- Melee hits: scrPlayerIsAttacking and scrPlayerIsPunching run every Step. They shift the player 12px forward, then `with (objEnemy)` tests place_meeting(x,y,objPlayer) and reads objPlayer.lastx/dir (scrPlayerIsAttacking.gml:1-8, 310-330).
- Guns: each shot spawns objBullet (speed 16, random spread), objShell and a muzzle flash (scrPlayerShoot.gml:360-392), and calls scrHearPlayer.

5) Executions: scrKillShield sets global.executionx/y (lines 11-12), then the player instance_destroy()s itself and is replaced by an objPlayer-child kill object chosen by scrGetKill(sprite). When the animation ends, that object instance_create()s a brand-new objPlayerMouse with the weapon sprite (e.g. objPKnifeKill_Step_0.gml:27-41). The same destroy/recreate pattern is used for windows, climbing, vomit and unlocking doors, so the player instance id is not stable.

6) Doors: objDoorV/objDoorH Collision_98 sets swingspeed=±8 based on which side the player is on. The door Step swings it, and the door's own Collision_275 handles enemies hit by it. objPlayerMouse's collision code entry named Collision_210 (objects.tsv says the object has Collision_99/100/210) breaks doors in hard mode with mask 4.

7) Death: enemy bullets hit the player through objPlayerMouse_Collision_209. It handles energie and hit count; on death it creates objPlayerDead (sprite_index, image_index, direction, speed, image_angle), drops objMaskDrop, drops the weapon as objWeaponThrow, then instance_destroy(). Melee deaths come from scrPlayerDieMelee, which runs `with (objPlayer)`. In total there are 64 objPlayerDead creation sites in 47 files. Restart: once no objPlayer exists, objEffector's R handler sets fade=1/next=0, and the fade end calls room_restart() (objEffector_Step_0.gml:443-547). Floor transitions: objTransitioner_Collision_98 sets objPlayer.persistent=true and objEffector.next=1/nextroom, and saves global.weaponsprite/ammoweapon/throwindex.

8) Masks are global (global.maskindex/maskon, copied into the instance's maskindex/maskon) and change player behaviour directly:
- 9: energie 3/5 (Create:88-94, 123-129). 21: energie 1.
- 5: speed 3.5 and sledgehammer impact ×2.35. 16: speed 4.
- 20: reversed controls. 7: George whole-room camera.
- 2: knuckles. 6: F-key knives. 22: chainsaw sprint.
- 27: Igel, no lock-on. 26: shader. 13 in hard mode: dies when the combo runs out (Step:408-444).
scrDrawMask draws using global.maskindex and global.selectskin[], not the instance's maskindex.

9) Logic also lives in Draw: objPlayerMouse_Draw_0 decrements reload and light (lines 66-77) and updates mask offsets through scrUpdateMaskPos when the sprite changes. The camera (view_xview/yview/angle[0]) is written directly by the player Step (lines 296-364) and by objPlayerDead_Step_0 (lines 289-312).

key_objects.name: objPlayer (idx 98)
key_objects.role: Abstract parent of 101 objects. It is the group almost all game code targets (objPlayer.x, with(objPlayer), instance_exists(objPlayer), place_meeting(...,objPlayer), Collision_98 events). Its own events are trivial and never inherited.

key_objects.name: objPlayerMouse (idx 0)
key_objects.role: Main in-level Jacket body, placed in 67 rooms. It handles input, aim, camera, combat, pickup, enemy-bullet damage and drawing (legs, body, mask, hot/fire/glow layers). It is recreated by about 116 files.

key_objects.name: Core player scripts
key_objects.role: Movement (scrPlayerMoveKeyboard), melee and guns (scrPlayerShoot, 54 sprite cases), melee hit detection (scrPlayerIsAttacking, scrPlayerIsPunching), animation return to walk sprites with `left` flip (scrPlayerAnimationEnd), executions, throat stab and human shield (scrKillShield, scrThroatEnemy, scrGetKill), pickup/throw/drop (scrPlayerPickUp, scrPlayerPickUp2, scrGetWeapon, scrCurrentWeapon/Ext, scrNoweapon), mask drawing (scrDrawMask, scrUpdateMaskPos, scrInitMaskPos), draw extras (script520 = scrDrawPlayerFire, script521 = scrDrawPlayerSkippy, script522 = scrDrawPlayerHot).

key_objects.name: objEffector
key_objects.role: Per-level manager. It computes global.mousex/mousey (aim point) from objPlayer.x and the display mouse, draws the cursor, handles lock-on redirection, fades, room_restart on R (only when no objPlayer exists), next-floor transitions via nextroom, score saves, and pause.

key_objects.name: objPlayerDead (idx 50) / objPlayerBombDead (51)
key_objects.role: Corpse. It slides with friction, bleeds, runs head-blow gore, moves the camera to the body, and starts a restart on R. Its Create is the single choke point for every player death.

key_objects.name: Execution / kill objects (about 70 objPlayer children, e.g. objPKnifeKill, objPKillFat*, objAubreyKill*, objMCKnifeKill, objPAttackThroat)
key_objects.role: Temporary player body during a ground finish. Each draws the victim sprite (`enemy`) plus the player sprite and mask (scrDrawMask(1)), and awards score/combo. At the end it instance_create()s a fresh objPlayerMouse with the weapon sprite and reload=30.

key_objects.name: objPlayerShieldMouse (idx 3)
key_objects.role: Human-shield body created by scrKillShield when holding a gun over an objKnockedOut. Speed 2.5, energie 10. Shoots via scrPlayerShieldShoot (Mouse_50) and drops the shield via Mouse_54. Shift held here is real look-far (aim = keyboard_check(vk_shift)).

key_objects.name: Story/character variants

single_player_assumptions.problem: The aim point is one global, computed by objEffector from the first objPlayer and the local hardware mouse.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Store per-player aimx/aimy. The local player sets them from the mouse; a remote player or puppet gets dir from the network and skips this line (guard with `if (net_is_remote) ...`).

single_player_assumptions.problem: `objPlayer.x` resolves to the first instance of any objPlayer child (GMS1 picks the first one found; the order is uncertain), so the cursor may anchor on the remote body.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Use global.localPlayer (instance id of the local body, refreshed every time it is recreated) instead of objPlayer here and in objEffector_Draw_0 lines 23-64.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Direct keyboard polling inside the body. Any second objPlayerMouse would also move with the local keys.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Replace with per-instance input fields (in_left/in_right/in_up/in_down) filled by the local input sampler or the network, or run this only for the local body.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Global mouse events (Mouse_50/51/55/57, KeyPress_32, Keyboard_70) fire for every instance of the object, so a second real objPlayerMouse would shoot, execute and pick up on the local player's clicks.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Add `if (id != global.localPlayer) exit;` at the top of each input event. Drive remote bodies by calling the same scripts from network handlers, or use a non-input puppet object.

single_player_assumptions.problem: The camera (view 0) is written by the player Step (lines 296-364), and also in Other_4.gml:40-44 and objPlayerDead_Step_0.gml:304-311.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Gate all view_* writes with a local-player check. The remote player's camera lives on the remote PC.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Object-wide field access plus global melee energy. objEffector_Step_0.gml:190-196 also mirrors it.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Use self.meleeenergie and make meleeenergie per-player state.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Level completion is decided inside the player's Step. Two bodies would double-spawn objCheckpoint, and the client would decide it locally.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Run only on the host's local player, or move it into a host-only manager and replicate global.done.

single_player_assumptions.problem: It runs inside with(objWeapon) and assigns the weapon to the first objPlayer instance, not the one that picked it up (the same applies to objPlayer.ammo in scrPlayerPickUp.gml:491-497 and scrPlayerPickUp2.gml:80).
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Set global.pickupper = id before with(objWeapon) and write global.pickupper.sprite_index/ammo. The tests point_distance(x,y,objPlayer.x,objPlayer.y) at scrPlayerPickUp.gml:453 and scrPlayerPickUp2.gml:47 need the same change.

single_player_assumptions.code: if (place_meeting(x, y, objPlayer) || place_meeting(x + global.spacex, y + global.spacey, objPlayer)) ... objPlayer.x = objPlayer.lastx;
single_player_assumptions.problem: Melee hit detection inside with(objEnemy) tests against any objPlayer and reads or writes the first instance's lastx/lasty/dir (86 objPlayer references in this script).
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Replace objPlayer with global.my_id (already set to the attacker at line 9) everywhere in the script.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Inside with(objKnockedOut), the execution type and weapon are read from the first objPlayer. Lines 11-12 use single global.executionx/y, and lines 519/576 spawn the dropped weapon at objPlayer.x.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Capture the attacker id in a global before the with-block and use it. Make executionx/y per-player, stored on the kill object.

single_player_assumptions.problem: About 116 files (133 sites) recreate a fresh objPlayerMouse after executions or transitions. Network identity, the local-or-remote flag and per-player state are lost on every finish.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Carry an `owner`/`pid` variable: copy it from the destroyed body into the kill object and from the kill object into the new body (or set it in objPlayerMouse Create from global.pendingOwner). Refresh global.localPlayer in objPlayerMouse Create.

single_player_assumptions.problem: An enemy melee hit kills every objPlayer instance, not the one actually hit.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Pass the target (nearest or colliding player) and use with(target). The same applies to scrPlayerDieDogBite, scrPlayerDiePantherBite and scrPlayerShieldDie*.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Restart is allowed only when no player exists. With a real second body, one player could never restart after dying alone; with a puppet, each PC restarts independently.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Make it host-authoritative: restart when both are dead (or on vote), then broadcast a 'restart' message so both clients run room_restart in the same frame. objPlayerDead_Step_0.gml:1-4 restart polling needs the same gate.

single_player_assumptions.code: objPlayer.persistent = true; objPlayer.addx = addx * 3; ... objEffector.next = 1; objEffector.nextroom = nextroom;
single_player_assumptions.problem: One player touching the exit moves the whole level and makes only the first objPlayer persistent. Weapon carry-over uses global.weaponsprite (single). The same happens in objTeleporter_Collision_98 and objElevator_Step_0 (lines 110-111, 141, 216-218, 291, 341).
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Host decides the transition and broadcasts nextroom. Each client makes its own local body persistent and saves its weapon in per-player globals. The puppet is recreated after the room change.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Duplicate-player cleanup in instance creation code (also code5320, code5331-5336, gml_RoomCC_rmHotel2_123316_Create, gml_RoomCC_rmMansionMainHall_121774_Create; 12 files). A second objPlayer-child body would make placed players destroy themselves.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Change to count only local bodies (e.g. a loop over objPlayer counting owner==local), or keep the remote puppet outside the objPlayer hierarchy.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Mask visuals and all mask gameplay effects read global.maskindex/maskon, so both players are forced to the same mask.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: For the puppet, temporarily swap global.maskindex/maskon/selectskin to the remote's values around scrDrawMask, then restore. For gameplay, accept a shared mask in v1 or refactor the reads to instance maskindex.

single_player_assumptions.problem: There is a single lock-on target. objEffector_Draw_0.gml:88-92 overrides the aim point with it, and objPlayerMouse_Create_0.gml:134 resets it on every respawn.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Keep it local-only on each PC (do not network it), and never let the puppet's Create reset it. The puppet should not be an objPlayerMouse.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Enemy AI targets the first objPlayer (the same in scrChasePlayer, scrEMeleeStep.gml:11-60, scrHearPlayer, objEnemy_Step_0.gml:30-32 and about 30 AI scripts).
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Add scrTargetPlayer() returning the nearest visible of (local body, remote puppet) on the host, and replace objPlayer.x/y in AI scripts with target.x/target.y.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Gameplay timers are decremented in Draw, so copying this Draw onto a puppet would also tick fire-rate state.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: The puppet Draw should copy only the draw_* calls (lines 1-65, 78-132 minus the timer lines). Keep reload authoritative on the owner.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Room-start bootstrap (objEffector, objBackgroundColor, objSurfacer, view placement) is done by the player body.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Only the local body should run it; the puppet must not.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Create also resets many globals (global.enemy, global.dog, global.deadIgel, global.pigkill, global.rasmusEm*) and forces the mask in rmTutorial/rmGriffin.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Never instantiate objPlayerMouse as the remote puppet. If a second real body is used, guard the global resets with an is-local check.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Enemy-bullet damage is a collision event on each concrete player object (objPlayerMouse, Biker, Griffin, ShieldMouse, MouseHouse, PigButcher, Controller), not on the objPlayer parent. A non-player puppet is never hit.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Give the host-side puppet its own collision with objEBullet (209) that sends 'you were hit (bullets, edir)' to the owning client, or that kills the puppet authoritatively and tells the client.

single_player_assumptions.code: with (objWeapon) { if (point_distance(x, y, objPlayer.x, objPlayer.y) < 32) { ... global.test = 2; } } ... objEffector.action = global.test;
single_player_assumptions.problem: Cursor pickup hints use the first objPlayer and a single objEffector.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Use the local player id only.

hook_points.file: NEW object objNetCoop (persistent, placed in or created from rmEnableSteam / Game Start, next to objConsole)
hook_points.purpose: external_define the transport DLL (ty_real/ty_string only). Begin Step: poll and dispatch received messages. End Step: snapshot global.localPlayer state (x, y, sprite_index, image_index, dir, left, legindex, legdir, light, HotWeaponAlpha, throwindex, object_index, maskindex/maskon) and send. Keeps global.localPlayer and the remote puppet id.

hook_points.file: NEW object objNetPuppet (NOT a child of objPlayer)
hook_points.purpose: Remote body: interpolates x/y and draws it by copying the draw calls from gml_Object_objPlayerMouse_Draw_0.gml (legs, body, scrDrawMask with swapped globals, script522 hot layer). On the host, add a Collision with objEBullet and route it to an AI target helper. Keeping it out of objPlayer avoids the 4217 objPlayer references, the 26 Collision_98 handlers and the duplicate-killer creation code.

Set global.localPlayer = id (or an owner tag) on every recreate, since about 116 files instance_create a new objPlayerMouse after executions, windows and transitions. The same applies to the Create events of objPlayerBiker, objPlayerGriffin, objPigButcher, objPlayerShieldMouse, objPlayerMouseHouse and objPlayerHospital.

After each objBullet / objExplosion / objFlame / objNail instance_create, emit a 'shot' event (weapon sprite, origin, direction(s), speed) so the host spawns authoritative bullets at the puppet, or the client mirrors cosmetic ones.
Host-side melee resolution: run it for the puppet on the host using a swing event (attack sprite, image_index, dir, x, y). Replace objPlayer with global.my_id inside the with(objEnemy) blocks.
Execution, throat-stab and human-shield entry point (Space). Emit an 'execute victim X with kill object scrGetKill(sprite)' event and get host approval of the victim id.
Weapon pickup, swap and throw (right-click release). Emit pickup (objWeapon id) and throw (objWeaponThrow params) events. scrPlayerPickUp2.gml and scrGetWeapon.gml need the same.

Single choke point for all 64 death sites. Broadcast 'player died' plus the corpse sprite, image_index, direction, speed, image_angle and image_yscale (read them one step later, since callers set them after instance_create).

Restart request. Route it to the host and restart when both are dead or on host command. Also patch the room_restart path in gml_Object_objEffector_Step_0.gml lines 443-547 so both PCs restart together.

HIERARCHY (decompiled\meta\objects.tsv): objEnemy (275) has 50 descendants: the main types objEnemy, objEnemyPatrol 276, objEnemyStationary 277, objEnemyMelee 278, objEnemyMeleeStationary 279, objEnemyFat 281, objEFatGunner 1220, objDogPatrol 282, objPolice 285 (7 children), objInspector 290, objChief 952, objEHideM16 280, objEnemyAmbush 1162, objEDodger 1224 and objEDodgerG 1221 (plus Patrol variants 1276/1277), and the abstract objEnemyIdle 332 (17 idle-pose children). objBoss 310 (16 children) and objNPC 306 (7) are abstract parents with no events. Several enemies have no parent: objSwat, objPanther, objESubwayStatic, objPrisoner, objClubOwner, objDoctorPatrol, objGuardRead, objBoss3, objFatman*. No enemy code calls event_inherited. A child that defines an event replaces the parent's event entirely; a child without it inherits objEnemy's events. Because of that, objEnemy_Collision_208 (the bullet hit) covers most children. The *Old objects and objEnemyMobile appear in no room and are never instance_created (rooms.txt, grep), so they are dead code. Rooms hold 910 placed enemy-like instances across 76 rooms, at most 39 per room (rmGallery), and room speed is 60.

CODE ENTRY NAMES: some are stale or renamed by the mod. objEnemy's Collision_1161 is in gml_Object_objEnemy_Collision_1147.gml, Collision_1264 (nail) is in gml_Object_objEnemy_Collision_0.gml, and Collision_1174 (flame) is in gml_Object_EnemyBurning.gml. objEDodger's code is in gml_Object_objEnemyDodger_*. objEnemySitIdle2 = objEnemySit2_*, and objEFatGiveUp = objFatGiveUp_*. I inferred these from the code, not from a linkage table.

AI STATE MACHINE (variable alert):
- alert 0 = idle/patrol. objEnemy wanders randomly via Alarm_0 (random(360), random speed). Patrol enemies follow walls via scrPatrol. Stationary enemies return home via scrReturn.
- Perception runs in scrSearch / scrMeleeSearch / scrDogSearch, throttled by checkreload (global.limitreload: 30 normal, 15 hard). The check runs if the distance to objPlayer is under 280 (100 with mask 18), or whenever the enemy is moving. scrLook ray-marches toward the player and returns 0 for clear line of sight, 1 for blocked, 2 for seen through glass or furniture.
- A clear sight starts alertwait=15 frames of reaction delay, then alert 1 (charge and shoot via scrCharge, or melee via scrAttack).
- Seen through glass gives alert 2: stand and aim (scrAim). Melee enemies instead path toward the player.
- Lost sight while alert>0 gives alert 3: mp_grid path to the player's CURRENT position with random jitter (scrChase), then a search animation at the end of the path.
- alert 4/5 = run to an objEHideTrigger, then become objEHideM16.

HEARING: scrHearPlayer is called from the player's shooting code. It sends up to 3 enemies within 295 px (90 with mask 12) on mp_grid paths to random points near objPlayer.

ATTACKS:
- Guns: scrEnemyShoot spawns objEBullet with random spread and speed, plus shells, sound and global.shake. The damage itself is applied in the player's own Collision_209 event, so it already works per player instance.
- Melee: the enemy's own Step checks place_meeting(ahead, objPlayer), then sets global.my_id=id and calls scrPlayerDieMelee. Dogs (and objPanther via scrPlayerDiePantherBite) work the same way. These scripts run with(objPlayer), which kills EVERY player.

DAMAGE AND DEATH:
- Player bullets → objEnemy_Collision_208: energie -= 1+caliber+bullet. Death happens if bullets>1 OR round(random(1)) OR energie<0, so it is a random roll.
- Nails, flame and explosions have their own entries.
- Melee → scrPlayerIsAttacking. A lethal weapon makes an objDeadBody inline; a blunt weapon or punch makes objKnockedOut via scrPlayerIsPunching.
- Doors (objDoorV/H Collision_275) and thrown weapons (objWeaponThrow_Step_0, which calls scrEnemyDieMelee) also knock down or kill.
- objKnockedOut counts down reload and plays a get-up animation. Its Other_7 then instance_creates the original type with sprEWalkUnarmed, and that enemy walks to the nearest weapon (scrGoGetWeapon).
- Executions are done by player-side objects that are children of objPlayer (objPBluntKill etc.).

DEATH OUTPUT: every death creates an objDeadBody (random sprite and frame, slides with friction, leaves blood sleds). It also creates objBloodDrop/objBloodSmoke/gore pieces, an objScore popup and global score/combo updates. If armed, the enemy drops objWeaponThrow with image_index=scrCurrentWeaponExt(sprite_index), ammo=ammo and a random direction and speed. Police also drop objPoliceHat, the phone enemy drops objCellPhone, and objEnemySitDrink drops a bottle. Blood decals are baked into surfaces by addToSurface; objDeadBody is explicitly excluded, so bodies stay as instances.

IDENTITY CHURN: enemies constantly instance_destroy themselves and instance_create a successor of a possibly different, randomly chosen type. This happens on idle→alert, unarmed→armed, knockdown→get-up, dog-bite end, the hide trigger, and the ambush trigger. Instance IDs are therefore not stable.

LOCKSTEP VS HOST-AUTHORITATIVE: there is a single global RNG, seeded with randomize() in gml_Room_rmEnableSteam_Create.gml and never with random_set_seed. Enemy code has about 2200 random/choose calls, and 39 enemy Draw events call random() for shake and light jitter. Lockstep or dual simulation is therefore infeasible.

Host-authoritative AI with client puppets IS feasible. Every enemy Draw event depends only on a small variable set: sprite_index, image_index, x, y, direction or angle, image_xscale/yscale, image_blend/alpha, shake, light, lastsprite, plus a few boss-specific values. Their random() use is cosmetic only. The cost is that the client must suppress every Step, Alarm, Collision and Animation End event, path and built-in motion on puppets, and must route its own player's hits to the host.

maps.counts: Enemy family, AI scripts and player-kill scripts: 662 code entries scanned. Of those, 161 files contain 1403 objPlayer* tokens: 351 objPlayer.x, 355 objPlayer.y, 169 instance_exists(objPlayer), 149 objPlayer.sprite_index, 95 with(objPlayer*), 23 place_meeting(...objPlayer), 18 objPlayer.persistent, 12 objPlayer.object_index. objPlayerMouse appears 65 times and objPlayerMouseHouse 28 times inside enemy and boss objects. AI scripts alone hold 302 objPlayer* tokens. instance_nearest is never used on objPlayer in enemy code; every reference is the first-instance form objPlayer.<var>. Families: objEnemy has 50 descendants, objEnemyIdle 17, objPolice 7, objBoss 16, objNPC 7. The family files contain about 2203 random/choose/random_range/irandom calls: Create 253, Step 732, Alarm 38, Collision 972, Other 53, Draw 106 (39 Draw events call random()). Rooms place 910 enemy-like instances in 76 rooms, at most 39 in one room. 73 with(objEnemy) loops exist game-wide, in 112 files that reference objEnemy. scrPlayerDie* is called from 18 object Step events.
risks: Single global RNG with no seeding beyond randomize() at boot (gml_Room_rmEnableSteam_Create.gml L2), with random() called even inside Draw events. Running the AI on both machines would desync within frames, so only host-authoritative AI is viable.

Enemy identities churn: about 15 kinds of code instance_destroy an enemy and instance_create a successor, sometimes of a random type (idle wake-up, weapon pickup, get-up, dog bite, hide/ambush triggers, objEnemyMelee hardmode swap). The network layer must track logical enemies with its own IDs and spawn/despawn messages, not GML instance IDs.

Client-local interactions with puppets would mutate the client world: its bullets trigger objEnemy_Collision_208, its melee (scrPlayerIsAttacking with(objEnemy)), doors (objDoorV_Collision_275), thrown weapons (objWeaponThrow_Step_0) and lean-execution checks (objKnockedOut_Step_0) would kill or knock down puppets locally, creating bodies, weapon drops and score. Every such site must become a hit request to the host, or a client prediction that the host confirms.

Room-start divergence: room-placed enemies run Create, Room Start and creation code on both machines with random weapon choice (objEnemy_Create_0 L35/39, objEnemyMelee_Create_0 L27, objPolice_Other_4), random energie, alarms and image_index. The host must send authoritative initial state for every enemy, or the client must not simulate room-placed enemies at all.

Puppet suppression is wide: no enemy code calls event_inherited and nearly every child defines its own Step, Other_7, Alarm and sometimes Collision. Gating has to be injected into hundreds of entries (Step entries alone ~100 files) or handled by replacing client enemies with a generic puppet object. Built-in motion (speed, path_start) and image_speed animation also run with Step suppressed and must be zeroed on puppets.

Bosses are tightly scripted single-player cutscenes. They convert the player object, toggle objPlayer.persistent around room changes, move view_xview[0], set global.done, and handle the restart key. Each boss needs its own co-op design; a mechanical replacement of objPlayer will not suffice.

Masks and difficulty change AI behavior (global.maskindex 3/10/12/15/18 and global.hardmode in Create, Step and sensing) and enemy weapons. The two players' differing masks would make simulation inconsistent unless the host's values govern the AI.

CPU cost: scrLook toggles solid on every furniture, door and soft wall instance per call and ray-marches. Evaluating LOS against 2 players doubles the cost for 39-enemy rooms; per-target throttling with checkreload is needed.

Score, combo and multiplier are single global variables updated inside enemy code (global.myscore, global.combo, global.kills, global.killx[], global.factor += sign(alert) in every enemy Step, reset by objSurfacer_Step_0 L1). Co-op needs an attribution rule (shared or per player) and host authority.

Level clear depends on exact enemy counts (objPlayerMouse_Step_0 L224 counts objEnemy+objKnockedOut+objECrawl+objMiscEnemy+objBoss+objEHideM16+objEBullet). Puppets that linger or duplicate on the client would block or trigger STAGE CLEAR incorrectly, so it must be host-decided.

If the remote player's proxy on the host is made an objPlayer child to reuse existing code, every untouched objPlayer.<var> resolves to one arbitrary instance. Enemies would silently focus one player, and code that writes objPlayer.x, objPlayer.sprite_index or objPlayer.persistent would corrupt the proxy.
open_questions: Does this GMS1 runner (build 1763) give room-placed instances the same instance IDs on every load and on both machines? If yes, they can serve as initial net IDs; runtime-created instances diverge either way. Verify at runtime.

The mapping of mod-renamed code entries to events is inferred from content (gml_Object_EnemyBurning.gml as objEnemy's objFlame collision, gml_Object_objEnemy_Collision_0.gml as the objNail collision, objEnemyDodger_* as objEDodger). For objEDodger/objEDodgerG, objects.tsv lists collisions (1164, 1174, 235, 61, 150...) with no matching files. Their event-to-code linkage should be dumped from UndertaleModTool before patching.
Should client kills be predicted (instant feedback, host confirms) or host-only (the client sees a delay of one round trip)? HM1's one-hit kills make latency very noticeable.

Should a player killed by an enemy die on the host's decision (host sends a death message with killer sprite and pdir) or on the victim client's local check against puppets? The kill scripts pick the death sprite from global.my_id.sprite_index, so the message must carry the killer's sprite.

Which player's global.maskindex/global.hardmode governs enemy generation and senses (mask 3 weapons, mask 12 hearing, mask 15 one-hit, mask 18 vision)? Mask 26 is cosmetic shader only and can stay local.

How should boss cutscenes behave with two players (objPlayerMouse → objPlayerMouseHouse conversions, objPlayer.persistent toggles, view_xview control in objChief/objBoss3Dead/objBigIgel/objBurningGuy)? Freeze both players, or only the closest?
Is scrLook's cost acceptable when run against 2 targets in 39-enemy rooms? This needs profiling; the hostile throttle (checkreload/global.limitreload) may need to alternate targets per check.

Generic puppet object vs. keeping the original objects with gated events: a puppet could reuse each original Draw via event_perform_object(net_obj, ev_draw, 0), but those Draws read and write instance vars (shake, light, lastsprite, HotWeaponAlpha, sound in objJonesBoss_Draw_0 L35-38 plays a sound). Behavior of event_perform_object on this runner needs verification.

maps.subsystem: Weapons, projectiles, damage, pickups and effects
maps.summary: The player's current weapon has no separate weapon ID. It is stored in the player's sprite_index: a walk sprite like sprPWalkM16 means "holding an M16" and sprPAttackM16 means "firing it". The only other weapon state is the instance variable ammo, plus throwindex for throwables (sprPWalkThrow) and HotWeaponAlpha for overheating. Weapons on the ground (objWeapon, objSpecificWeapon, and objWeaponThrow while flying) store the weapon type as image_index, a frame of sprWeapons. gml_Script_scrIndexNameWeapon.gml lists the names: 0=M16, 1=Shotgun, 2=Golf Club, 3=Pipe, 4=Bat, 5=Knife ... 26=Chainsaw, 30-37 throwables, 39 Shorty, 40 M60, 41 Flamethrower, 42 Nailgun, 45 Aks, 52 RPG. scrCurrentWeaponExt(sprite) converts a sprite to an index (it uses raw numeric sprite ids and falls back to objPlayer.throwindex). scrGetWeapon (run with an objWeapon as self) converts an index back by writing objPlayer.sprite_index. Max ammo comes from scrGunIndexGetMaxAmmo. objWeapon_Create_0 picks a RANDOM image_index (lines 2-6), so the guns lying in a room differ between machines unless the host sends them. Firing goes through one script: global left button held (objPlayerMouse_Mouse_50) calls gml_Script_scrPlayerShoot.gml, which switches on sprite_index across about 54 cases. Each case sets reload (M16 3, Uzi 3, MP5 4, M60 4+rand, Kalashnikov/Aks 6, Silencer/DoubleBarrel/Shorty 12, 9mm/Magnum 14, Shotgun 30, Hunting Rifle 40, flamethrower 0). Guns also do ammo -= 1 and set impact/impside recoil. If place_meeting(objSolid/objDoorV) is true 10-12px in front, the gun spawns objSmokeHit instead of a bullet and may push a door. Otherwise it creates objBullet at x+lengthdir(16..26, dir-7..dir+2). Spread is uniform: direction = dir - a + random(2a). The shotgun fires 8 pellets and DoubleBarrel/Shorty fire 16 pellets with speed 16-random(4..6). Mask 15 changes spread and enables ricochet. caliber=1 (Hunting Rifle, Magnum) makes a bullet pass through enemies. reload is decremented in objPlayerMouse_Draw_0 (lines 66-69), not in Step. Attack sprites drop out of the switch until scrPlayerAnimationEnd restores the walk sprite, so the real fire rate is max(reload, length of the attack animation). Other weapons spawn special objects: objFlame (flamethrower, one per frame), objNail, objWaterBullet (Toy MP5), objBulletSkippy/objBulletSkippyLaser, objPWater (boiling pot) and, for the RPG, an objExplosion with RPGJOKE=1 placed at global.mousex/mousey. Throwables become objThrowingWeapon, and dropping or throwing a gun or melee weapon (scrPlayerPickUp, right-button release) creates objWeaponThrow. A thrown weapon moving with speed>2.5 knocks enemies into objKnockedOut, or kills them for knives, pool cue and similar. When it stops it turns back into objWeapon (objWeaponThrow_Step_0 lines 2-21). Melee has NO hitbox object. While the attack sprite plays, scrPlayerIsAttacking and scrPlayerIsPunching move the player instance 12px along dir and run with(objEnemy) place_meeting(x,y,objPlayer) to kill or knock out whatever they touch, then move the player back. Bullets themselves contain no enemy-damage code. Enemies handle the hit in objEnemy_Collision_208: energie -= 1+caliber+bullet, and the enemy dies if bullets>1, if round(random(1)) succeeds (50%), or if energie<0. A dying enemy spawns objDeadBody and gore, drops objWeaponThrow(scrCurrentWeaponExt(sprite), ammo) and adds the global score. objBullet only hits enemies, never players, so there is no friendly fire. Players are hit by objEBullet (75 player-state objects have Collision_209). objPlayerMouse_Collision_209 does energie -= 1, and the player dies if bullets>1, if a 50% roll succeeds, or if energie<0 (masks 9/21 act as armor). On death it creates objPlayerDead plus objMaskDrop plus objWeaponThrow and destroys the player. Doors (objDoorV and children) are swing physics using swingspeed, image_angle and swinger. A player touching a door sets swingspeed ±8 and swinger=1, and a door swinging with |swingspeed|>3.5 knocks any enemy it hits into objKnockedOut and drops its weapon (objDoorV_Collision_275). Executions are not hitboxes either. Space calls scrKillShield, which picks an overlapping objKnockedOut and calls scrGetKill(sprite_index), which returns an execution object such as 8=objEnemyBash or 29=objPKnifeKill. It then destroys the player and the knocked-out enemy. The execution object is itself an objPlayer child and runs on global mouse events. objEnemyBash's Create rolls energie=1+floor(random(4)) clicks. When the execution ends it creates a fresh objPlayerMouse, keeping the weapon through global.willemweapon/willemammo. objEnemyBash and objEnemyHeadKick are therefore confirmed to be PLAYER execution states despite their names: both have parent objPlayer (objects.tsv rows 8 and 9).

key_objects.name: scrPlayerShoot (script)
key_objects.role: The one gameplay firing routine. It switches on the player's sprite_index (about 54 cases), sets reload, ammo, recoil (impact/impside), sounds, shake and muzzle, and spawns objBullet/objFlame/objNail/objWaterBullet/objBulletSkippy*/objExplosion(RPG)/objThrowingWeapon/objPWater plus cosmetic objShell/objSmokeHit/objMuzzle. hook_points.purpose: The central place where gameplay projectiles are created. Before calling it (in Mouse_50, Mouse_51 and scrXboxPlayerShoot), get the next instance id by creating and destroying a dummy marker object. After it returns, collect every new projectile with id > marker from with(objBullet/objFlame/objWaterBullet/objPWater/objExplosion/objThrowingWeapon), reading object_index, x, y, direction, speed, image_angle, caliber, bullet, bullets, angle, wavelerp and RPGJOKE, and send one FIRE packet. The host recreates exactly those instances with owner=slot, so no RNG replay is needed.
Fire-input entry point (window special case plus scrPlayerShoot). On a client: run locally for feedback, mark the spawned bullets netghost=1, and send the FIRE packet.
Griffin 9mm fire (lines 1-37) and hold-right drop (scrPlayerPickUp2). Needs the same FIRE and DROP capture.
Pickup and throw (scrPlayerPickUp). Send PICKUP{weapon net id} or THROW{objWeaponThrow/objThrowingWeapon params}; the host validates and destroys the objWeapon.
Weapon acquired. Change it to take a target instance; on the host, apply it to the remote proxy when a PICKUP is accepted.

Execution start (scrKillShield). Send EXECUTE{victim knocked-out net id, scrGetKill result, image_angle, carried weapon/ammo}; the host removes the objKnockedOut and spawns the remote execution proxy.

risks: Code-entry file names do NOT reliably match the real event subtype or object index. Examples: objEnemy has events Collision_208/1161/1174/1264 but its files are Collision_208, Collision_0 (handles objNail), Collision_1147 (handles objEAmbushTrigger 1161), and the objFlame handler is gml_Object_EnemyBurning.gml. objThrowingWeapon_Collision_0 is really Collision_275 (objEnemy). objAubreyKill*_Collision_264 is really Collision_209. objPBluntKill_collision_20 is lowercase and nonstandard. objPlayerMouse lists Collision_99/100/210 events, but its Collision_210 file contains door-breaking code even though index 210 is objClip. Inject code by event in the UTMT object editor, never by file name.

Kill outcomes are decided by random(): enemies die from a single bullet on round(random(1)) (objEnemy_Collision_208 line 141), players likewise (objPlayerMouse_Collision_209 line 212). Execution click counts are random (objEnemyBash_Create line 5), knockdown get-up time is random (objKnockedOut_Create line 4) and ground weapons are random (objWeapon_Create lines 2-6). Without strict host authority every machine diverges.

The fire-rate timer (reload) decrements in Draw_0, and the effective fire rate also depends on attack-animation frame counts and image_speed. Re-simulating fire on the host from 'trigger held' input will not match the client; replicate the actual spawned projectiles instead.

Executions destroy the player instance and recreate objPlayerMouse at the end (about 60 objP*Kill objects). The player's instance id changes after every execution and after many scripted transitions, so the network identity must be a stable slot variable, not an instance id.

Weapon logic relies on global per-player state: global.maskindex/maskon/hardmode (spread, ricochet, armor, ammo multipliers), global.knives, global.meleeenergie, global.willemweapon/ammo, global.Skippy* and global.shake. Two players with different masks are impossible without refactoring.
Scratch globals are reused across scripts (global.my_id, global.test, global.dir, global.myx/myy). Injected network code must not depend on them persisting.

A host-side proxy that is a child of objPlayer automatically gets door pushes and enemy targeting. But every objPlayer.x reference (3427 occurrences) may then resolve to the proxy instead of the host's own player; GMS1 returns the 'first' instance in an unspecified order.

Child projectiles (objNail, objBulletSkippy, objBulletSkippyLaser) have their own Create without event_inherited, so any new variable such as netghost/netowner must be initialised in each Create. GMS 1.4 has no variable_instance_exists to probe for it safely (not referenced in meta/general.txt; verify).
The flamethrower has reload 0 and spawns objFlame every frame (scrPlayerShoot lines 1653-1676). Per-shot FIRE packets mean 60 msgs/s, so replicate it as a stream state (on/off, dir) instead.
Bullets are fast built-in motion (16 px/frame) with per-step overlap collisions. Ghost bullets on a client will visually pass through or hit things differently than the host's authoritative bullets.
objBullet_Collision_317 line 149 uses objBullet.caliber (the first bullet in the room) instead of self caliber. This is an existing bug, but it makes board damage nondeterministic between machines.

Collision events defined for both a parent and a child object (objEnemy has Collision_208 objBullet and Collision_1264 objNail) may both fire for a nail. Verify in the runner before relying on a single handler.

maps.subsystem: Level flow, rooms, progression, scoring, saves (Hotline Miami Super R-R, GMS1.4 build 1763)
maps.summary:
There are 164 rooms. Indices 0-152 are in the room order (meta/general.txt). Eleven mod rooms (153 rmRasmus ... 163 rmMadnessMorgue, including rmHotel1-3, rmOptions, rmMorgue, rmPoliceHQShootingRange) sit outside the order and are reached only through room_goto. Every room runs at 60 fps except rmPoliceHQShootingRange, which runs at 30 (meta/rooms.txt).

Story loop. The menu (objTitle_Draw_0.gml:96-102) sets global.level=0 and goes to rmTutorial (22). From there the order is rmPart (7) -> rmDream1 (19) -> an apartment rmSequenceN. Each apartment's room creation code (e.g. gml_Room_rmSequence1_Create.gml) sets global.level (the room index of the chapter's first floor), global.title/pretitle/sequence and global.done=0. The phone dialog (scrGetMessage) sets global.done/phone. The player then goes downstairs and touches the car (objPlayerCarEnter). With an apartment player, the car leads to rmChapter (12) if done, otherwise rmInterlude (8) -> a store chosen by scrCarNextInterlude.

Level start. rmChapter's objLevelTitle sets global.PauseRestart=1 and calls room_goto(global.level) (objLevelTitle_Draw_0.gml ~126-137). The level controller objEffector then runs a reset walk (objEffector_Step_0.gml:205-349):
- It jumps to the last floor, levelres. This comes from code5458.gml (= scrLevelRestart), a table mapping first floor to last floor.
- It walks back one room index at a time with room_goto(room - rmSplashScreen), i.e. room-1. On each floor it calls room_set_persistent(room,0)+room_restart, which wipes leftover state.
- On the first floor it zeroes all score globals.
So every level is a block of contiguous room indices, and hard-coded indices appear everywhere: scrCarNextRoom, scrGetSequence, the nextroom==16/4/42/8/7/12/13/88 checks.

Each floor room holds an objEffector-family controller (objEffector, or its children objEffectorHouse, objEffectorInstant, objEffectorHospital). Its Room Start calls room_set_persistent(room,1) (objEffector_Other_4.gml:10), so floors you return to keep their corpses.

Floor exits are objTransitioner, objTeleporter and objElevator. objTransitioner stays solid and invisible while any objEnemy/objKnockedOut/objBoss/objEHideM16/objESubwayStatic exists (objTransitioner_Step_0.gml:22-45). On touch (Collision_98 = objPlayer), it does the following (objTransitioner_Collision_98.gml:16-91):
- It makes the player persistent and sets the push-out vector addx/addy.
- It sets objEffector.next/fade/nextroom.
- It writes the floor checkpoint: every score global is copied to a *save twin, and the weapon is stored as global.weaponsprite/ammoweapon.
- The player carries its x,y into the next room. Each floor's room-placed player destroys itself if another objPlayer already exists (code5320.gml:4) and otherwise takes global.weaponsprite.

Fade timing. The fade-out runs 18 frames (amount 180->0 by 10). When it finishes, objEffector Step (lines 357-570) branches:
- restart==1: game_restart.
- next==1: room=nextroom.
- otherwise (death): turn off the room's persistence, room_restart, and copy the *save globals back. There is no game_save anywhere; scrCheckpoint only moves the view. Per-room exceptions (train station, SWAT, the boss checkpoints in objEffectorHouse_Draw_0.gml:645-765) respawn the player in place instead.

Restart. A death creates objPlayerDead. Pressing R only restarts when no objPlayer instance exists (objEffector_KeyPress_82.gml:5).

Floor and level clear:
- objPlayerMouse_Step_0.gml:219-262 spawns the "STAGE CLEAR" banner (objCheckpoint) once its enemy-count test hits 0.
- scrCheckMissionComplete (called every Step) and about 60 boss/phone objects set global.done=1 (with done1..done4 for multi-wing levels) and create objLevelComplete.
- The HUD then shows "GO TO CAR" (scrDrawHUD.gml:445-510).
- The car (objPlayerCarEnter_Step_0.gml:40-176) needs place_meeting(objPlayer) && global.done. It routes through scrCarNextRoom, normally to rmScore (16).

Scoring. All scoring is global and single-copy. Enemy death code writes global.myscore/killscore/boldscore/combo/combotime=240/kills and adds strings to the global.bonuslist ds_list (about 120 files). The combo timer decays, and the combo payout happens, inside scrDrawHUD (Draw event). global.time also ticks in objEffector Draw.

Grading and branching:
- rmScore's objScoreStats sums the 7 bonus categories plus global.totalscore. It decides global.newguns from the save data.
- rmScoreDetails grades against scrGetMaxpoints(title). It saves global.grade/highscore and picks the next room from local unlock state: 11 = mask unlock, 18 = weapon unlock, otherwise scrGetSequence -> the next store/apartment.

Saves are plain text and ini files per machine:
- saves.dat (scrSaveUnlocked: masks, levels, guns, grades, highscores; written at rmChapter and on the score/unlock screens).
- options.ini (trunk weapon), Achievements.ini, mask.nfo (the chosen mask; re-read after every floor restart through global.maskload -> scrLoadMask).
- Marker files: skip, hardmode, restartmusic, gameunlock, and others.

Pause is a real room. ESC sets global.lastroom and Post-Draw copies application_surface. The game then switches to rmPause (index 9), the level room surviving because it is persistent. Resume sets room=global.lastroom with global.paused=1 so Room Start skips its setup. Restart from the pause menu re-runs the PauseRestart backward walk. Quit calls game_restart.

Dialog runs through objPhoneConversation (created by scrGetMessage*). It advances on the global left-click event (Mouse_53), and holding the right button (Mouse_51) skips it.

Persistent helper objects are created once in rmEnableSteam: objRoomCheck, objConsole (dev console with room_goto), objControlHud, objRasmusHud, objAchievementsHud and others. game_restart sends the game back to rmEnableSteam -> rmSplashScreen -> rmMenu (through the "skip" file).

single_player_assumptions.code: objPlayer.persistent = true; objPlayer.addx = addx * 3; objPlayer.addy = addy * 3;
single_player_assumptions.problem: Object-name assignment touches every objPlayer instance, so a remote proxy that is an objPlayer child would also become persistent. The checkpoint weapon is read only from objPlayerMouse (lines 45-91). Any player touching the stairs ends the floor for everyone.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Gate on host. Store the toucher id and use with(toucher). Snapshot both players' loadouts (P1 and P2 copies of weaponsprite/ammoweapon). Send ROOM_CHANGE carrying the arrival x/y so the partner is placed next to the toucher.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Same single-player pattern as the transitioner (also used by objElevator_Step_0.gml ~150-200 and objHospitalTransitioner_Collision_98.gml:6-11).
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Same host-gated transition script shared by all exit objects.

single_player_assumptions.problem: The room-placed player kills itself whenever any other objPlayer exists. With a persistent or proxy P2 counted as objPlayer, P1 would vanish after room_restart. The same check is in code5330/5336.gml, gml_RoomCC_rmMansionMainHall_121774_Create.gml:1 and gml_RoomCC_rmHotel2_123316_Create.gml:4, and code5331-5333 for the hospital.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Count only local-player instances (e.g. a variable is_local), or make the remote proxy not a child of objPlayer. Spawn P2 next to the placed P1 spawn point.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Restart is allowed only when no player exists at all. With a living partner, the dead player can never restart, and a proxy objPlayer would block it too. The same check is in objPlayerDead_Step_0.gml:1-4, objEffector_Step_0.gml:126-129, objEffectorHouse_KeyPress_82.gml:1, scrXboxRestart.gml and scrXboxEffectorStart.gml.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Replace with a co-op rule: the client sends RESTART_REQUEST; the host decides (both dead, or the shared-life rule) and broadcasts RESTART_FLOOR.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Death restart restores one global snapshot and restarts the room locally. Both machines must do this together, and the client must not trigger it itself.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Run this only on a host RESTART_FLOOR message, including the *save snapshot from the host so both restore identical values.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Local room change after the fade. Up to 113 direct room-change call sites (53 files) can each make one machine leave the room alone.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Route every change through scrNetRoomGoto(target, kind). The host broadcasts; the client moves only on the host's command and treats its own local triggers as requests.

single_player_assumptions.code: switch (global.PauseRestart) { case 1: room_goto(levelres); ... case 2: ... room_goto(room - rmSplashScreen);
single_player_assumptions.problem: Level start and restart walk backward through every floor to clear room persistence. The client must reproduce this exactly, or its floors keep stale corpses and enemies.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Send LEVEL_START/RESTART_LEVEL and let each machine run the deterministic walk locally (no per-step handshake). Sync with a READY barrier once room == global.level.

single_player_assumptions.code: global.lastroom = room; room_persistent = true; shouldscreenshot = 1; (then Draw_77: room = rmPause)
single_player_assumptions.problem: Pause leaves the level room. The paused machine freezes its simulation while the other continues, and the persistent room is resumed with global.paused=1.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: In co-op, either pause both (the host broadcasts PAUSE/RESUME and both go to rmPause and back), or replace it with a non-room overlay menu that does not stop the simulation. The same entry points are objEffectorHouse_KeyPress_27.gml, objEffectorHospital_KeyPress_27.gml and scrXboxEffector*Pause.gml.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Pause-menu Restart and Quit (objPause_Draw_0.gml:86 game_restart) are local.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Host only: send RESTART_LEVEL. Quit on the client should mean disconnect; quit on the host returns both to the menu.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Any objPlayer touching the car ends the level. It then manipulates objPlayer.y/sprite_index (lines 90-95), which hits the first or every instance.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Host only. Optionally require both living players near the car, and broadcast CAR_EXIT.

single_player_assumptions.code: if (clear == 0 && global.done == 0 && ...) { clear = 1; my_id = instance_create(x, y, objCheckpoint); ...
single_player_assumptions.problem: Floor-clear detection runs per player instance from local enemy counts. Two local player objects would spawn two banners, and client enemy proxies counted late would cause an early or late clear.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Do the clear check only on the host for the local P1, and broadcast FLOOR_CLEAR. On the client, drive objTransitioner.solid/visible from the host flag.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Called every Step (objEffector_Step_0.gml:197). It derives level completion from local instance counts.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Run it on the host only and replicate global.done/done1-4 to the client.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Combo decay and payout run in the Draw event on each machine. The client would pay out combos on its own and spawn objScore popups at objPlayer.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: On the client, skip lines 2-101 and use the host's combo/combotime/comboscore values. Show the popup from a host event.

single_player_assumptions.problem: The level timer (time bonus = (18000 - time)*0.5) ticks locally and pauses differently per machine.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Host-owned; the client overwrites it from the snapshot.

single_player_assumptions.code: vdist = point_distance(objPlayer.x, objPlayer.y, room_width / 2, room_height / 2); ... view_angle[0] = ...
single_player_assumptions.problem: Camera tilt and cursor (Draw_0.gml:7-99) use objPlayer, i.e. whichever instance comes first, not the local player. The same happens in scrCheckpoint.gml:3-24 and objPlayerMouse_Other_4.gml:40-49.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Use a global.localplayer instance id for view and cursor math on each machine.

single_player_assumptions.problem: Every player instance sets view[0] at Room Start, so a P2 proxy would hijack P1's camera.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Do this only for the local player.

single_player_assumptions.code: global.maskindex = select; objPlayer.maskindex = select; ... if (global.maskindex == 10) with (objEnemy) ammo = ceil(ammo * 1.33);
single_player_assumptions.problem: There is one global mask, and it changes world rules (enemy ammo, mask 13 hard-mode kill timer in objEffector_Step_0.gml:613-651, the mask 14 HUD). mask.nfo is a single file, and scrLoadMask applies it with(objPlayer) to all players.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Split into a host world mask (global.maskindex) and a per-player mask (playermask). The client tells the host its mask; the host applies world effects only from P1's mask (or the mask union by design).

single_player_assumptions.problem: The mask-13 hard-mode combo-timeout kill hits every player instance.
single_player_assumptions.fix_idea: Target only the host's mask owner, or decide by co-op rule.

risks: Pause is a room change to rmPause (index 9), relying on room persistence and global.paused=1. Unless both machines pause together, the simulations diverge immediately, and the resumed room skips Room Start init.

Level start and restart walk backward through every floor (PauseRestart 1->2, room_goto(room-1) with room_set_persistent(room,0) and room_restart). This depends on contiguous room indices and code5458 (scrLevelRestart). A desynced or missed step leaves stale persistent floors on the client.

Hard-coded room indices are everywhere (scrCarNextRoom, scrGetSequence, scrGetRoom, the nextroom==16/4/42/8/7/12/13/88 cursurf checks, room - rmSplashScreen). Any GML injection that inserts or reorders rooms in data.win breaks progression; new rooms must go at the end.
Floors are persistent (objEffector_Other_4.gml:10), so revisiting a floor restores local state. The client's corpses and weapon drops must match the host's, or host and client diverge on revisits.

Per-machine save data (saves.dat masks/levels/totalscore, options.ini trunk weapon, mask.nfo) feeds branching (objScoreDetails next=11/18, objScoreStats newguns, the level-select unlock check, the car trunk weapon). The client must follow host commands rather than compute its own next room.

game_restart (10 sites) is used as 'quit to menu' and for bonus-level ends (scrCarNextRoom sets restart=1). It destroys all instances, including any persistent net manager, and resets globals. The DLL must keep its socket across it, or the flow must be replaced with room_goto(rmMenu) in co-op.

Many transitions run in Draw events (objEffectorHouse Draw, objLevelTitle/objScoreStats/objScoreDetails/objPause/objDizzy Draw). If the runner skips Draw while a window is minimized or unfocused, that machine's transition stalls (unverified).
Floor transitions keep the toucher's x,y because floors are aligned near the stairs. The partner's x,y may be inside walls on the next floor, so the partner must be teleported to the arrival point.

Object-name dot assignment (objPlayer.persistent/addx/maskindex/...) affects every instance. Making the remote player an objPlayer child affects transitions, the self-destruct creation code (code5320 etc.), restart gating, camera and mask code. Not making it a child breaks enemy targeting, which belongs to a different subsystem. This is a central design decision.

Score and combo are computed inside enemy-death code (about 120 files) and in Draw (scrDrawHUD). The client must not run enemy-death scoring for proxy enemies, or score is counted twice locally (it would only be overwritten by the snapshot if the snapshot is authoritative and frequent).

Special-case death restarts (rmTrainstationEntrance with the train, rmSwatDownstairs after done, rmHouse1Downstairs/rmOfficeEntrance boss checkpoints, rmMansionMainHall) recreate one player at fixed or checkpoint coordinates instead of calling room_restart. Each needs co-op handling.
rmPoliceHQShootingRange runs at room_speed 30 while every other room runs at 60, so step-based net timing must handle the change.
The dev console (objConsole, persistent) and objSkip (persistent, right-click hold) can change rooms or skip cutscenes locally.

maps.summary:
All files below are in C:\Users\kopiy\Downloads\Super_R-R\decompiled\CodeEntries.

1. The game has no engine-driven camera. No code uses view_object (the room-view settings themselves are not in meta/rooms.txt, so this is not confirmed). The view is moved only by script, through view_xview[0], view_yview[0], view_angle[0] and view_wview[0]/view_hview[0]: 79 code entries write xview/yview and 68 write view_angle.

2. Each active player-state object moves the camera from its own Step event. In objPlayerMouse_Step_0.gml:296-364 the view centre eases 10% per frame toward x+lengthdir(24,dir). When Shift (aimfar, line 268) or global.ShiftLook is on, it eases instead toward objPlayer.x + (display_mouse_get_x()-display_get_width()/2)*view_wview/display_get_width()*factor (factor 2 for the hunting rifle). Mask 7 (George) lerps to fixed per-room cameras from scrGeorgeCam. The same block is copied into objPlayerBiker, objPlayerGriffin, objPigButcher, objPlayerShieldMouse, objPlayerMouseHouse, objPlayerHospital, the window objects and several execution objects (e.g. objPAttackThroat_Step_0.gml:84-91).

3. On Room Start (objPlayerMouse_Other_4.gml:29-50) the view snaps to the player, offset 20% toward the room centre. The same event creates objEffector, objBackgroundColor and objSurfacer if they are missing. Persistent players carry xview/yview and vlastx across room transitions.

4. objEffector (index 89, depth -9999, sprite sprCursor) is the camera post-processor, the cursor, the HUD host and the level-flow controller.
   - Its Step (objEffector_Step_0.gml:571-659) saves vlastx/vlasty as the pre-shake view.
   - It adds a random offset of ±global.shake, turns shake into global.angleshake and zoom, then decays shake by 0.5 per frame.
   - It sets the tilt: view_angle = lengthdir_y(vdist*0.00625, vdir*2) + angleshake, where vdist/vdir are objPlayer's distance and direction from the room centre.
   - scrHardMode adds 180 degrees in hard mode.
   - It sets view_wview/view_hview = global.wview/global.hview minus the zoom.

5. objEffector Draw (objEffector_Draw_0.gml):
   - It recomputes the cursor and draws it with angle -view_angle so it stays upright.
   - It switches to a screen-space projection, d3d_set_projection_ortho(0,0,global.viewwview,global.viewhview,0), for the HUD, fades, scanlines, vignette (scrScreenFilterEffector) and siren tint.
   - At lines 337-342 it restores the projection and resets view_xview to vlastx, so shake lasts one frame.

6. The variants objEffectorHouse (64 rooms), objEffectorInstant (14) and objEffectorHospital (4) are children that fully override Step and Draw. None of them calls event_inherited, so the cursor, shake and HUD code is duplicated four times.

7. Cursor and aim never use mouse_x/mouse_y in gameplay.
   - global.mousex/mousey = objPlayer.x + (display_mouse_get_x()-display_get_width()/2)*view_wview/display_get_width()*factor, with factor 1.8 when Shift is held (objEffector_Draw_0.gml:69-82). The offset is negated in hard mode.
   - So the cursor is anchored to the player, uses world axes, and ignores both the view position and view_angle.
   - Lock-on (objPlayerMouse_Mouse_55.gml, global middle-press) stores global.enemy. The Draw then replaces global.mousex/y with the enemy's position (objEffector_Draw_0.gml:86-99).
   - dir = point_direction(x,y,global.mousex,global.mousey) (objPlayerMouse_Step_0.gml:58) is therefore already a world-space angle. The remote player's aim should be sent as dir plus the world aim point and lock target, never as raw mouse values.

8. Player rendering (objPlayerMouse_Draw_0.gml) draws a light circle, legs, body and mask. scrDrawMask reads global.maskindex and global.selectskin, and the Skippy glow comes from global.GlowSkippy, global.PShaking and related globals.
   - The same Draw counts down gameplay timers: reload, debuffammo and light (lines 66-77).
   - The Biker, Griffin, PigButcher, Shield, MouseHouse and Hospital Draw events also recompute dir from global.mousex.
   - scrDrawPlayer redraws persistent (transitioning) players in screen space, and also recomputes dir from global.mousex.

9. HUD: scrDrawHUD (objEffector) and scrStoryDrawAmmo (objEffectorHouse) draw the score, ammo and combo, plus the restart prompt via scrDrawRestartHLM2.
   - The score animates global.drawscore toward global.myscore. Ammo is derived from objPlayer.sprite_index, objPlayer.ammo and objPlayer.object_index. The combo is drawn by scrComboLine.
   - They also run gameplay inside Draw: the combo timer countdown, comboscore, objScore pop-ups and achievements. objEffector Draw also advances global.time.

10. Screen effects:
   - global.shake (173 files write it), global.blink and global.comboflash.
   - objBackgroundColor (depth 9999999) draws a world-space quad around the view.
   - objSurfacer draws the blood/corpse surfaces global.surface[cursurf] at 1/3 scale.
   - The lighting engines draw subtractive light surfaces offset by the view, with light circles from `with (objPlayer)`.
   - The mask-26 palette shaders shd_russell_* are toggled by the global mask.
   - objHLM1Scanlines and objHLM2Noise draw in Draw GUI.

11. For co-op, three things matter most:
   - Every PC already renders its own view, so the camera only has to stop being moved by the remote player.
   - Today `objPlayer.x/.y` is used for the camera, tilt, cursor and HUD. With two objPlayer-family instances, it resolves to whichever instance comes first.
   - Room Start, checkpoint and mask-menu snaps loop `with (objPlayer)`. The death, gib and cutscene objects grab the camera unconditionally.

12. Recommended design: make the remote player a dedicated puppet object, child of objPlayer but with its own Step and Draw, so none of the copied state-machine camera code runs for it. Then:
   - Replace objPlayer references in camera, cursor and HUD code with a global local-player handle, kept up to date across the ~133 objPlayerMouse re-creations.
   - Gate the death camera with a remote flag.

risks: Gameplay logic lives in Draw events. This includes the combo timer and comboscore (scrDrawHUD.gml:2-101), global.time (objEffector_Draw_0.gml:198), reload/light/debuffammo countdowns and dir recomputation in the player Draw events, room changes in objEffectorHouse_Draw_0.gml:590-640, and objTrailFire creation in script520. If a client runs them for puppets, or a PC skips Draw (e.g. while minimized, unverified), state diverges.

objPlayer.x/y and objPlayer.var resolve to the first instance in GMS1's instance list. With a remote objPlayer-family puppet present, the camera tilt, cursor anchor, shift-look and HUD ammo can silently switch to the remote player. The 1411 objPlayer.x/y references go far beyond camera code.

Many non-player objects grab the camera unconditionally: death and gib objects, boss/cutscene objects (objChief, objClubOwner, objPrisoner, objSacrifice, objPoliceHardTrigger, objVan, objOldman, objJanitor*, objJonesBoss, objBigIgel, objTrain), scrCheckpoint and objMaskMenu. In co-op, events caused by the other player steal the local camera, and cutscenes may also convert the puppet into a real objPlayerMouse.
Every room-start, checkpoint and mask-menu snap that uses `with (objPlayer)` iterates both players, so the camera ends up on whichever runs last.
The camera is updated incrementally (view += lengthdir(viewspeed)), so a stray write by a remote-owned object cannot simply be overwritten later without keeping our own copy of the camera position.

objEffector (and its variants) also owns level flow: fade, room change, restart, pause. Boss scripts destroy and recreate it. Cursor and HUD instance state (leveltitle, ammox, pluscombo, action) resets whenever that happens.
Pause is a room change to rmPause (objEffector_KeyPress_27.gml, objEffector_Draw_77.gml) and is incompatible with a shared live level.
objConsole Step sets room_speed to 30 when the window is unfocused (gml_Object_objconsole_Step_0.gml:52-59), changing the tick rate on one PC.

Input is read as hardware state regardless of focus (display_mouse_get_x, keyboard_check_direct(vk_shift), global mouse events). Two instances on one PC for testing will both react to the same mouse and keys.

Per-player cosmetics are global (mask, skin, Skippy glow, PhotoNegativeCircle, global.maddx, mask-26 shaders): the remote player will be drawn with the local player's mask and palette unless these are made per-instance.

Hard mode rotates the view 180 degrees and negates the cursor offset in roughly 20 duplicated branches. World-space aim stays correct, but each camera block has a hard-mode copy that must be patched too.

The mask 7 George camera (scrGeorgeCam, objPlayerMouse_Step_0.gml:336-362) replaces follow with fixed per-room views and widens view_wview/hview. Global camera width is fine per PC, but its logic is tied to global.maskindex.

global.shake is shared by any code that runs on the PC. If remote-player actions are re-simulated locally (scrPlayerShoot, executions), the local screen shakes for the partner's shots. That may or may not be desired.
open_questions: Room view definitions (view 0 size, view_object follow target, hborder/vborder, port size) are not in meta/rooms.txt. Check in UndertaleModTool whether any room's view 0 has a follow object; if so, the engine would also follow the first objPlayer instance.

GMS1 Step order between objPlayerMouse and objEffector: objEffector Step captures vlastx after the player's follow, assuming the player's Step runs first. The player has the lower object index and objEffector is usually created in the player's Room Start, but the runner's actual ordering (creation order vs object index) for build 1763 should be verified, especially for objEffector instances pre-placed in 56 rooms.
Does the GMS 1.x runner (build 1763) keep executing Draw events while the window is minimized or occluded? A lot of gameplay is in Draw (see risks).

Will the remote player be a dedicated puppet object (recommended: child of objPlayer with its own Step/Draw, so enemies can target it while the copied camera code never runs for it), or a real objPlayerMouse/state-machine instance (then every camera block in 25+ player objects needs a local check, and a local flag must survive ~133 instance swaps)?
Is variable_instance_exists / variable_instance_get available in this runner build, to tag instances safely? Otherwise use object_index checks or a global local-player id.
What should the local camera do when the local player is dead and the partner is alive? Currently objPlayerDead locks the camera on the corpse and the HUD shows 'PRESS R TO RESTART'.

Is the hardware cursor hidden through Global Game Settings (no window_set_cursor call exists in GML)? This matters only for local presentation.

maps.subsystem: Engine infrastructure: boot/init chain, persistent controllers, globals, timing, RNG, external DLLs, input config, console, Steam/networking presence, FUNC-chunk availability, and hook points for the co-op DLL, net pump and host/join menu
maps.summary:
All paths below are relative to C:\Users\kopiy\Downloads\Super_R-R. I re-checked a previous partial run (coop_notes/map_partial_run2.json, "map:infra") against the code and corrected several of its claims.

Boot chain. The first room is rmEnableSteam (index 0, meta/rooms.txt lines 1-10). It holds the persistent controllers objRoomCheck, objControlHud, objWindowsMouseLock, objWindowedMode, objLanguage, objConsole, objAchievementsHud and objRasmusHud, plus the non-persistent objSteamQuestion. Its creation code (gml_Room_rmEnableSteam_Create.gml) does room_goto_next(); randomize(); and resets global.cc, gotbeaten and locked, so the Steam question screen is never visible. objLanguage_Create_0 sets global.language=0 and calls global_init(), which is code entry gml_Script_script458 (mapping in meta/general.txt line 615). global_init external_defines CleanMem.dll (halo_shg_clean/halo_shg_get_mem) and sets player_lock, god, notarget, restart, strah, rickhitted and snd. This is the earliest gameplay-independent code, and it runs again on every game_restart().

Splash and menu. rmSplashScreen's objSplashScreen_Create_0 reads or creates options.ini into globals. It external_defines LowPassFilter.dll (line 50), runs scrSongINIT (script494, which external_calls LowPassFilter with 4 args, 2 of them strings) and forces window_set_fullscreen(true) (line 66). It sets global.locked=1 if AlienInMiami.dll is missing (line 92); with locked=1 the Draw event calls game_end() (Draw_0 line 95). A 'skip' flag file jumps straight to rmMenu (line 106); otherwise the flow is rmDevolver, then rmDennatonSplash, then rmMenu. In rmMenu, objTitle_Create_0 swaps itself for objTitleNew when global.main_menu_new is set (default 1). Both call scrTitleInit, which re-initializes about 150 run globals, surfaces, cleanmem_init, the optional GMXInput (only if an 'xbox' file exists), the optional AlienInMiami init (only if an 'alienware' file exists), scrLoadKeys, unlocks and achievements on every menu entry. The menu has 4 hard-coded items. The room switch happens in objTitleNew_Draw_0 lines 134-172: START GAME goes to room 22 (rmTutorial), CHAPTERS to rmLevelSelect, OPTIONS to rmOptions (room 159, one of the mod rooms 153-163, which are not in the room order and are reached only by index), and EXIT calls game_end().

Console. objConsole is a mod developer console. It is toggled with F5 only when options.ini console=1 (objConsole_KeyPress_116), and sets global.player_lock while open. objConsole_Other_11 is a 1242-line command interpreter: god, noclip, teleport, killthemall, object/global setvar via variable_global_set/variable_local_set, level next/restart/goto, timescale, key binds and more. KeyPress_1 replays bound commands from the binds.txt ds_map. The console has NO external_define of its own. It only external_calls the CleanMem handles from global_init: memory stats in Other_11 lines 31/63, and EmptyWorkingSet on every Room Start in Other_4 line 7. Other_4 also calls game_set_speed(60, gamespeed_fps) every Room Start. objconsole_Step_0 lines 52-59 set room_speed=30 when the window lacks focus and 60 otherwise. objConsole_Other_11 line 1237 marks any cheat use with global.cheater=1.

Timing is purely frame-based at 60 steps/s. Every room is speed 60 except mod room rmPoliceHQShootingRange [162] at 30, which objConsole forces back to 60. delta_time is unused and not even in VARI. The 'sleep' script is a no-op loop. A few timers use wall-clock current_time: objExplosion_Step_0 lines 58/328, objTrainshake_Step_0, objBikeEnding.

RNG. randomize() is called exactly once per boot (rmEnableSteam creation code). random_set_seed and random_get_seed are referenced nowhere and are not in the FUNC chunk. Randomness is pervasive: random() 7980 times in 1570 files, choose() 643 times in 364 files, random_range 405 times. That includes 661 Create files, 272 Step files and 165 Draw files (546 calls), so cosmetic draws consume the shared RNG. Lockstep is infeasible, and host-authoritative is required.

Input. There are no joystick_*/gamepad_* calls. The gamepad is only reachable through GMXInput.dll wrappers (dllinit/checkbutton/leftthumb_x...), and that DLL is not shipped. Movement uses keyboard_check_direct(ord(global.upkey/leftkey/downkey/rightkey)) in scrPlayerMoveKeyboard (lines 124-171). Keys are 5 letters stored in keyboard.dat (scrLoadKeys/scrSaveKeys) and edited in objShowControls (rmControls, reached from Options 'CONTROLS SCHEME' nextrm=6 or from the legacy objTitle). Aim is the single pair global.mousex/global.mousey, computed in objEffector_Draw_0 lines 75-81 from display_mouse_get_x/y around objPlayer. World interactions use GLOBAL mouse events plus place_meeting(objPlayer): 66 Mouse_53 and 42 Mouse_54 entries, for example objKeycard_Mouse_54.

DLLs and Steam. CleanMem.dll is a 1 KB stub that imports only OpenProcess, EmptyWorkingSet and GetProcessMemoryInfo. LowPassFilter.dll uses sndfile.dll. AlienInMiami.dll is the original Dennaton AlienFX DLL: exports AlienInitialize, AlienRelease, AlienRotatePink, AlienRotateYellow and DeathBlink; it LoadLibraryA's LightFX.dll, starts threads with _beginthreadex, needs MSVCR100/MSVCP100, and has no hooking imports (no VirtualProtect, WriteProcessMemory or SetWindowsHookEx). The mod only checks that the file exists (anti-tamper gate). AlienInitialize is called only if an 'alienware' flag file exists (scrTitleInit lines 54-58); objAlienWare is placed in no room. Steamworks.dll, GMXInput.dll, Oddio.dll and vcapture.dll are absent. Every Steam* wrapper script starts with if (global.steamon), and steamdll_init itself sets global.steamon=0 (line 17), so Steam is effectively always off. GEN8 has SteamAppID=0 and the SteamEnabled flag unset, and no native steam_* function appears anywhere, so the missing steam_api.dll is harmless.

Networking presence: no network_* in code or FUNC, no Async (Other_68) event, and async_load is not in VARI. buffer_create, buffer_exists and buffer_delete are in FUNC (833 entries) but appear in no decompiled code. GLOB and EXTN chunks are empty. The runner exe (Oct 2016, GMS 1.4.1763) imports WS2_32 and contains network_*, buffer_get_address, random_set_seed, parameter_string, window_set_caption, delta_time, joystick_* and gamepad_*. The earlier UTMT probe (_work/recompile_test.win) added 0 FUNC entries and 1 CodeLocals entry, so calling a built-in not already in FUNC is still unverified.

Corrections to the previous run:
- The DLL cleanup blocks in objOptions_Draw_0 (lines 121-155) and objBandCredits_Draw_0 (lines 95-129) run on EVERY exit from Options or credits back to rmMenu, not on game exit. Do not put coop_shutdown there.
- global.locked is overloaded. It is the AlienInMiami-missing flag at boot and the keycard/door lock state in levels (objKeycard_Mouse_54, rmHospitalTopFloor/rmPoliceHQFloor3 creation code).
- The objConsole Draw_64 code (listed in meta/objects.tsv) has no matching decompiled file, and some code-entry names do not match their event: objTitleNew_Mouse_0.gml exists, while objects.tsv lists Mouse_53. Verify event bindings in UTMT before patching by file name.
